answer: The forest is counted without felling it: cruisers sample random plots and scale the stand from them, so knowing the timber never costs the timber. Logs enter the flume at the one marked inlet, each tagged, and tags ride the water to the mill - one route, all accounted. Across the baseline the surveyor's mirror talks in flashes: heliotrope glints at set instants pin the triangulation, geometry confirmed by light with no cargo. Farms clear-cut to count, dump logs untagged, and flash whenever it suits them. Honest agents sample, tag, flash on schedule - and let the stand keep standing.
